questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was something very different from what I'm used to.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Everything is super convenient in China. Staff at UNNC were really informative and always replied me fast on mail. People in general will go out of their way to help you with the english they know.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were mentors who received us new international exchange students, that we had been contacted by before coming. They helped us with accommodation and other check-in procedures.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Two options for exchange students: A private room with its own bathroom (building 11) or private room with shared bathroom and common area (building 20)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were no cooking facilities what so ever. However, food is super cheep at campus, so that was no problem.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is waaay nicer to live in building 11 than 20. B11 is new, whilst B20 is not really nice at all, but I believe it will be renovated within the next couple of years.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in building 20

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They are not that good at English again, but people are super friendly to help

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was really organized. You received a paper that included around 4-5 steps, that told what taks to complete at different stations

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guidance from the mentors and if you just ask people that you see nearby, then they will help you as well

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes that I wanted, so completely successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it and have some patience

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level does not measure up to the standarts at social sciences at University of Copenhagen, however I know other people from other majors had a different experience.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was actually pretty similar

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
INTS4106 Global International Relations
INTS4016 International Institutions and Networks
CHIN4031 Contemporary China Issues 
INTS4013 Research Methods

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend Global International Relations and Contemporary China Issues. The first one really challenges the IR field as we know it in the West. The latter is just a really good way to learn interesting things about China

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Just all the wonderful traveling I got to do

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is so soo cheap here, so I got a lot of things

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really great oppertunities, especially for sports. They have a sportscenter which is free, where you can attend classes or go to the gym, or rent your own volleyball/tennisball court etc - also for free ;)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I mentioned the sports above. The university arranged many different cultural events and field trips, here amongst tea-leaf-picking-day in the mountains, lantern festival, opera and so many other things

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Maybe not a specific one, I tried many different things which was super fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend other students to travel as much as possible: Hangzhou, Suzhou, Shanghai and Huangshan are only a few hours away by train

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I mostly talked to other international students and the campus is very western-like, so there was not that much to adjust to

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Most local students come off as shy and may not speak English well. However, they are super sweet and I got a handful of local anyways

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing was particularly challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their kindness and openness to strangers

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: That you can go to China without knowing Chinese and everything will still be okay. However, the second most important thing to know is that their English is almost non-existent, which is why it is really good to have installed apps on your phone, I would recommend "Oversæt" since you also can take pictures of text, which it will translate for you. Now, about the host institution: Again, everything is super convenient here, so no worries at all

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just get the rights apps down on your phone: Wechat, Aplipay (to pay with and book trains/flights), Oversæt, LetsVPN, Navigator (I think its called), Taobao (to order things online)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know myself better and expanding my comfort zone. Getting friends from all over the world!!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Knowing when to give yourself a break from social life. People here surely like to go out and about

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
